_comment: Business buyers (sales channel 3). Once reputation reaches unlock_rep, companies email bulk orders and custom server builds; the player accepts or declines with one click (no haggling). Bulk: qty units of `type`, at least `grades` (one is picked), optional min RAM/storage (0 = any), paid unit_price each = the price_percentile guide of matching models at that grade × price_mult. Builds: chassis = model ids that can host it, cpus × one of cpu_ids, at least ram_gb (memory type from the chassis), drives × at least drive_gb, psus fitted, raid = a RAID controller; price = the cheapest parts for the spec at PartsHub prices (barebones chassis included) × price_mult. hours = working hours to deliver (+ hours_per_unit for bulk). qty scales up with reputation. Body placeholders: {company} {buyer} {qty} {things} {grade} {spec} {due} {unit_price} {total} {sign} {name} {spec_list} {price}.

welcome.subject: You're on the radar
welcome.body:
Alright,

Word gets round. A couple of people have asked me who does decent refurbished kit, and I've been giving them your name.

Businesses work differently from Flogit punters: they email in with a proper order — twenty laptops by Friday, that sort of thing — or a server built to a spec. Fixed price, take it or leave it, and they pay when it lands. Miss the deadline and they'll remember.

It's all in the new Business app on the office PC. The server builds are where the money is — hang on to good CPUs, memory and drives.

G
